newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: HOLYMAN SHARES DIVE AS INVESTORS JUMP SHIP.
newsitem.headline: HOLYMAN SHARES DIVE AS INVESTORS JUMP SHIP.

text.p: Shares in ferry operator Holyman Ltd slid to their lowest level in three years on Thursday as more investors deserted the stock following Wednesday's profit downgrade.
By 12.30 p.m. (0230 GMT), Holyman shares were over 23 percent lower at A$1.80 on turnover of 2.26 million shares.
On Wednesday Holyman said it had reduced its year net profit forecast to the range of A$11.5 million to A$13.5 million from a A$14 million to A$16 million range predicted on June 6.
"It's all been on the back of the downgrade," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank.
"It has been written up quite a bit and people have seen how weak the shares were yesterday."

Holyman cited a performance below expectations from its 67 percent owned U.K. division Holyman Sally as the reason for the downgrade, adding that half year profit to June 30 would be materially affected by Holyman Sally's results in that period.
The remainder of Holyman Sally is owned by Silja Oy Ab of Finland.
However, Holyman noted that excluding Holyman Sally, other units were performing in line with existing forecasts.

Holyman shares listed in April 1994 and reached a peak of A$6.00 in November 1996 before tumbling 70 percent to today's lows. By 12.50 p.m. (0250 GMT), Holyman shares were 55 cents lower at A$1.80 on turnover of 2.26 million.
